name: PromptRobust (Prompt-Perturbation Robustness Benchmark)
executive_summary: Measures how much a model's output changes under small, realistic prompt perturbations — typos, synonym swaps, sentence reordering, semantic paraphrase — across 4,788 adversarial prompts over 8 tasks and 13 datasets.
description: Distinct from the security-focused prompt-injection/jailbreak literature elsewhere in this catalog: PromptRobust isn't about malicious attackers, it's about ordinary robustness to the kind of small variation real users introduce unintentionally (character-level typos, word-level synonym substitution, sentence-level reordering, and semantic-level paraphrase). Evaluates across sentiment analysis, natural language inference, reading comprehension, machine translation, and math problem-solving, revealing that current LLMs are considerably more sensitive to small input perturbations than their headline benchmark accuracy would suggest, and provides prompt-composition recommendations to reduce that sensitivity.
when_to_use: Evaluating whether a deployed prompt's performance is robust to realistic user-introduced variation (typos, rephrasing) before shipping, not just accurate on a clean test set.
Comparing candidate prompt phrasings not just for peak accuracy but for stability under small perturbations.
when_not_to_use: Threat-modeling deliberate, adversarial manipulation — see the prompt-injection/jailbreak entries in this same category for that distinct threat model.
known_pitfalls: A prompt can score well on a clean benchmark while being fragile under this kind of perturbation testing — the two properties are measured separately and don't imply each other.

primary_source.authors: Zhu, Wang, Zhou, Wang, Chen, Wang, Yang, Ye, Zhang, Gong, Xie
primary_source.title: PromptRobust: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Large Language Models on Adversarial Prompts
primary_source.venue: ACM Workshop on Large AI Systems and Models with Privacy and Safety Analysis (LAMPS) 2024

usage_templates.template:
Base prompt: {{base_prompt}}
Generate perturbed variants at each level:
- Character-level: introduce {{num_typos}} realistic typos
- Word-level: substitute {{num_synonym_swaps}} words with synonyms
- Sentence-level: reorder sentences where order isn't semantically required
- Semantic-level: paraphrase the whole prompt while preserving meaning
Run the target model on the base prompt and all perturbed variants against the same {{eval_examples}}. Report the spread in output/accuracy across variants — a large spread indicates a fragile prompt even if the base prompt's own accuracy looks good.

variables.name: num_typos
variables.description: How many character-level perturbations to introduce

variables.name: num_synonym_swaps
variables.description: How many word-level substitutions to introduce

variables.name: eval_examples
variables.description: The evaluation examples run under each variant

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
